description: No RSS/API/structured feed identified for Службен весник, Собрание decisions, or NBRNM press releases; all candidates are HTML/PDF scrape targets.
Mid-level regulator personnel (directorate heads for supervision, payment systems, fintech/oversight, AML at NBRNM; unit heads at KHV) are not systematically published anywhere found.

Albanian-language (sq) sources were not searched, although Albanian is an official language in RNM and several regulator officeholders and outlets (e.g. Albanian-language media) publish appointment news in Albanian.
No historical succession dataset (governors, vice-governors, Council members with mandate start/end dates) was located in machine-readable form.
The President of RNM formally proposes the NBRNM Governor to the Assembly, but the presidency's own publication channel (pretsedatel.mk) was not directly examined in this pass.

The full list of licensed banks, savings houses, payment institutions and e-money institutions (with EMBS numbers) was not enumerated in this pass because the NBRSM register pages returned 403 to direct fetch.
Exact fee schedule and licensing terms for CRM current-status/history certificates and for the Интернет дистрибутивен систем were not confirmed beyond a reported ~5,000 MKD minimum prepayment.
Run languages were mk and en only; North Macedonia has substantial official Albanian-language publication, and some register/gazette material and issuer announcements appear in Albanian.

The CRM Регистар на годишни сметки (annual accounts register) was not examined; bank annual accounts and annual reports filed there disclose board composition and headcount, a secondary but legally compelled record.
NBRSM prior-consent decisions for bank board appointments are legally required but no public list of issued consents was located in this pass.
MBA's Комисии (commissions) and SKIBOR panel subpages were identified via site navigation but not fetched, so committee chairs and panel bank composition remain unknown.

The Chamber of North Macedonia's ~15 associations, ~12 asocijacii and ~38 groups were confirmed to exist as a numbered URL space but only two were inspected (ICT id=5, non-bank financial id=25; id=14 also surfaced).
AmCham's 130+ member roster and FIC's ~40-company membership were confirmed to exist as pages but were not fetched, so no actual member names were captured beyond board officers.

No insurance-sector association (e.g. an association of insurance companies or insurance brokers) was confirmed; only the regulator ISA/АСО (aso.mk) surfaced. Since the run scope is sector=both, an insurance-side association may exist and be unmapped.

Association governance changes (new board, new secretary) must be filed with the Central Registry of North Macedonia, but no registry-based verification path for association officers was explored in this pass.
Association secretariat hiring (analysts, project officers, EU-project staff such as MBA's MiCreS project) is not published on any confirmed source; only elected officers are visible.

The ESJN portal's own search interface, its CPV filtering, and whether anonymous users can browse concluded-contract detail pages (vs. needing a subscribed account) were not established, because the portal 403'd.

Municipal and public-enterprise contracting authorities (општини, ЈП Водовод, ЕСМ, Пошта на Северна Македонија, ФЗОМ, ПИОМ) were not individually enumerated, yet they are the volume buyers of card acceptance and e-payment collection.
IFI procurement routes outside the EU (EBRD, World Bank, EIB) that fund MK financial-sector and PFM work were referenced only in passing; their own procurement notice boards were not scouted.
Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, although Albanian is an official language and municipal contracting authorities in western MK publish in it.
No validated CPV code list for the payments/banking scope was assembled, and MK CPV usage was not observed on any real notice.
Seavus, ULTRA, Neotel, Semos and the Netcetera-adjacent Skopje payments houses have not been mapped to their own careers pages, client pages or MASIT profiles.
Leadership-move detection for vendors depends almost entirely on LinkedIn, which is login-walled and ToS-restricted for automated collection; no open substitute was found.

Albanian-language sources were not searched at all; a significant share of MK IT and banking employment activity (Tetovo, Gostivar, Struga, and Albanian-language business media) is invisible to mk+en-only coverage.

No authoritative registry source is yet wired in: the Central Registry of the Republic of North Macedonia (Централен регистар на РСМ) would give incorporation, activity code, management (управител) and annual-account data for every vendor in this cell.
The 'bank PDF supplier fingerprint' technique was identified but only sampled on Stopanska banka and CCB; it has not been applied systematically across all MK banks.
International scheme and vendor partner-locators (Mastercard/Visa partner directories, Microsoft/Oracle/Temenos/Finastra partner finders) were not searched for MK-registered partners.

The eCommerce Conference speaker archives were identified from search results but individual speaker pages were not fetched, so the exact schema (does each card carry title + employer + year?) is inferred, not confirmed.

Albanian-language (sq) event and academic sources in North Macedonia were not searched — a material share of MK banking/fintech staff and institutions (e.g. Tetovo/SEEU, Albanian-language business media) communicate in sq, and the run's language scope (mk, en) excludes it.

Individual bank 'awards & recognitions' and 'press/events' pages (Komercijalna, NLB, Stopanska, Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse, Silk Road, Centralna kooperativna, TTK) were not enumerated in this cell, although they publish which executive represented the bank at which conference.

Video channels were not covered: NBRNM's YouTube channel and MBA/conference organisers post full panel recordings whose titles and descriptions state speaker names and roles, often when no agenda PDF survives.

Conference sites routinely delete prior-year speaker pages when a new edition launches (the AETM site already splits editions across /2019/, /2020/, /2021/ and a 2022 subdomain). Title-drift analysis depends on those historical snapshots.
The richest single channel for speaker/title signal (LinkedIn pages of MBA, KIBS, banks and conference organisers) is auth-walled and ToS-restricted for automated collection.

СФОМ's per-bank member organisations, collective-agreement documents and news archive were only summarised at one level; individual bank union branches (e.g. синдикална организација при Комерцијална банка) were not enumerated with URLs.
The NBRSM report and indicator pages, which carry employees/branches per bank, could not be fetched or their document URLs enumerated.
No court/registry layer covered: Централен регистар на РСМ (management-board and authorised-person changes per bank) and labour-court judgments on dismissals were not searched in this cell.

Albanian-language labour and banking coverage (portalb.mk, koha.mk) was not searched, despite a substantial Albanian-speaking banking workforce and Halkbank/TEB-type institutions with Albanian-language communication.

Employer-side and job-market signals of organisation change (Агенција за вработување на РСМ vacancy statistics, vraboti.mk / pazaranarabota.mk bank job postings, LinkedIn bank headcount pages) were not covered in this cell.
No verified enumeration of archived 'Управен и Надзорен одбор' / management page URLs for the ~13 MK banks, because web.archive.org egress is blocked for this agent.

No international executive-search / HR-market source found for MK banking (no regional headhunter reports, no LinkedIn-derived aggregators, no salary/hiring trackers) covering the 'jobs' and 'hiring' topics as opposed to top-level 'leadership moves'.
The two highest-yield English sources for this cell (SeeNews, The Banker) and both major rating agencies are paywalled or login-walled; only headlines and syndicated mirrors are freely retrievable.

Payments-sector (non-bank) actors — CaSys, KIBS, Klikni Kupi, Nayax and card-scheme country managers — have no identified international monitor that reports their personnel changes; only one-off market-entry stories were found.

Albanian-language coverage (sq) was not searched — a significant share of MK banking-sector reporting and of the relevant labour pool is Albanian-language, and TEB/Halkbank-linked networks in particular are covered by sq-language outlets.
No first-party newsroom or management page was confirmed this pass for Централна кооперативна банка Скопје, Silk Road Bank, or ТТК Банка at the level of named Управен/Надзорен одбор rosters.

NBRM (Народна банка на РСМ) governor approvals of management/supervisory board appointments were referenced indirectly (Sparkasse SB re-appointments approved by the Governor) but the regulator's own approval notices were not scouted — they sit outside this cell but are the confirming leg for every appointment found here.

Only NLB (2016–2026 year tabs), Sparkasse (numbered AGM sessions) and the Silk Road legacy site (NewsDetails.php?News=N) offer an enumerable historical archive; the .nspx sites (kb.mk, pcb.mk, halkbank.mk) show no obvious pagination depth from the landing pages.

Careers pages were confirmed for KB, STB, NLB, Halkbank corporate and Silk Road, but not for Sparkasse, ProCredit, UNIBanka, TTK or CCBank — leaving the 'jobs/hiring' topic unevenly covered across the cell.

Sparkasse and CCBank serve Cyrillic-percent-encoded .aspx paths and deep /Upload/ PDF folders; TTK is query-string driven; Unibank stores AGM PDFs in space-and-Cyrillic folder names. Generic crawlers will mis-handle these URLs.

Only 7 banks appear on MSE mandatory listing. Foreign-owned banks with no free float (e.g. Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse, Silk Road) have no SEI-NET obligation, so their leadership changes never reach this feed.
The NBRM regime for granting consent to bank board members is documented, but no page listing individual granted consents with dates and names was located within this slice's budget.
Службен весник на РСМ (slvesnik.com.mk) was identified as a likely publication venue for regulator decisions but was not searched in this slice.
Централен депозитар за хартии од вредност (CSD) was not investigated; it may hold complementary issuer and shareholder-event records.
RSS gives only a recent window and the MSE announcement archive's filter grammar is not fully mapped, so multi-year backfill of governance filings is not yet designable.

The full licensed population of MK payment institutions and e-money institutions under the 2022 Law was not enumerated, because the NBRSM registers could not be fetched. Only four PSP/EMI actors were confirmed by name in media: Paysera Македонија, Iute Pay, Flex Pay (Флекс пеј), plus foreign entrant Nayax.

No MK-specific general job board (e.g. vrabotuvanje.com.mk, pazar3.mk, mojarabota-type portals) was verified in this pass as carrying payments-sector vacancies; only fakulteti.mk and bankarstvo.mk were observed.

Bank-owned or telco-owned wallet/e-money ventures (Halkbank Skopje wallet, A1/Telekom-linked payment ventures, mPay/CPay-style wallets) were not confirmed as MK entities in this pass — the mPay hit was a non-MK app.
Annual reports / годишни извештаи of KIBS and CaSys (which list management and supervisory board composition year by year) were not located.
Albanian-language MK media were out of declared scope and therefore uncovered.
Visa's MK ownership chain is unresolved - no country-level Visa actor for MK was identified, only CEMEA-level roles.

The MK Central Registry (Централен регистар на РСМ), the primary filing source for officer/director changes at vendor subsidiaries, was not located or assessed in this run - only third-party aggregators (Club200, CompanyWall) were found.
No procurement/tender source was identified, despite tenders being the main observable trace for ATM and core-banking vendors in MK.
Vendor-side MK job ads were confirmed to be reachable in principle (vrabotuvanje.com.mk, it.mk/kariera, bankarstvo.mk job posts) but no specific vendor vacancy was actually retrieved in this run.
Albanian-language MK media were not searched, despite a substantial Albanian-speaking market segment in MK and the Mastercard cluster spanning Albania and Kosovo.
No dedicated Balkans fintech/payments trade publication was identified beyond the generalist SeeNews and the ATM-specific ATM Marketplace.
SeeNews, the strongest English pointer feed, is likely partially paywalled, and LinkedIn, the strongest personnel channel, is authwalled and ToS-restricted.

No historical archive or time-series of MK job ads was located. Job boards delete expired ads, so a vacancy observed today is unrecoverable in six months, and no backfill baseline exists to say whether current bank hiring is elevated or normal.

Individual career-page URLs were resolved for only one bank (Stopanska Banka). Komercijalna, NLB, Sparkasse, Halkbank, Silk Road, CKB, Kapital, ProCredit, and the PSP/processor set (CaSys, KIBS, Payten/Asseco, Iute) are known as actors but their own career endpoints were not individually pinned down in this pass.

The cell scope covers mk and en, but North Macedonia has a large Albanian-speaking population and banks (notably in Tetovo, Gostivar, Skopje) recruit in Albanian. No Albanian-language job board or Albanian-language vacancy channel was searched or identified.

No social-media vacancy channels were investigated. MK employers routinely post ads to Facebook pages and groups, and Telegram/Viber job groups are common; MojaPlata itself surfaced primarily via Facebook in search results.

No structural labour-market denominator for the financial sector was secured — e.g. State Statistical Office (Државен завод за статистика) employment-by-activity series or NBRSM banking-sector headcount reporting — against which vacancy counts could be normalised.

Only two URLs in this slice were actually fetched (bankarstvo.mk article, vrabotuvanje.com.mk banking search). All other URLs come from search-result metadata and are unverified for liveness, and no robots.txt was inspected for any domain.

The single most valuable object in this cell — the member-level 'new role' post and the profile Experience section — is behind login and effectively invisible to open search and to automated collection under LinkedIn's ToS.

LinkedIn company pages were confirmed for only 6 of the ~13-15 MK banks plus CaSys; Halkbank, Sparkasse, Stopanska, Komercijalna, Silk Road, Development Bank, Centralna kooperativna banka, and the savings houses are unmapped in this layer.
No time-series of company-page headcount or function mix exists; the People tab is only useful as a diff, and no baseline snapshot has been taken.

Macedonian-language coverage of the professional-network layer is thin because MK practitioners appear to use English for career announcements; Albanian-language sources (a significant MK professional community) were not covered at all in this cell.
Every high-value source in this cell involves personal data about identified individuals, and the obvious workaround sources (Datanyze/ZoomInfo/Lusha/AroundDeal) are scraped derivatives.
No URL in this slice was fetched or liveness-checked; all are recorded from search-result evidence only.

The layoff/restructuring lexicon for MK was not empirically validated — no article using redundancy vocabulary was found, so the working glossary ('отпуштања', 'реорганизација') may simply be the wrong register.

Turkish-language and Turkey-linked coverage is absent from this cell even though Halkbank AD Skopje and Ziraat are Turkish-owned and their executive appointments (e.g. the Halkbank CEO change observed on Bankarstvo) originate in Turkish parent-group announcements and Turkish business press.

This cell covers the media/commentary layer only. Every appointment story observed traced back to a National Bank (NBRM) consent decision or a Macedonian Stock Exchange (MSE) issuer announcement — the primary records that media merely report, often days later.

Two legacy archive domains were discovered (arhiva.emagazin.mk, arkiv.portalb.mk) indicating that historical MK/sq appointment coverage lives on separate hosts from current sites — a historical baseline of executive tenure is achievable but requires distinct crawls.

Executive names appear in Cyrillic (mk), Latin transliteration (en), and Albanian orthography (sq) with inconsistent spellings, and bank names have changed through mergers/rebrands (e.g. NLB Tutunska Banka to NLB Banka, KB Publikum Invest to KB Invest, Ohridska Banka).

The richest editorial depth in this cell (Kapital magazine, Ekonomija i Biznis) sits in print/PDF products rather than in crawlable article HTML, and LinkedIn — the natural corroborator for individual executive moves — is ToS-blocked for automated collection.
SEINet (MK issuer disclosures) and KAP (Turkish issuer disclosures) are both JS/session-driven and were not directly enumerated in this pass.

The Bulgarian (CCB Sofia / Chimimport / BSE-Sofia X3News) and Turkish (KAP) parent legs were searched but no subsidiary-specific filings were captured; Slovenian-language NLB releases were also not enumerated separately.
Sparkasse Bank Makedonija's news/press path and Halkbank AD Skopje's news path were not confirmed; only site roots are recorded.
Parent-group sources cover leadership and reorganisation well but give almost no signal on MK subsidiary hiring volumes or job postings.
Foreign-ownership map for smaller MK banks is prone to staleness in third-party sources.
